name: profile-close-window-light
prompt: Every gang member wears a knitted balaclava covering the whole head, with no eye, nose or mouth holes; a large white ring is stitched round the face, and a red triangle sits high over the wearer's left eye (on the right of the picture, at about 2 o'clock); gloves on both hands, collars and cuffs closed, no skin showing anywhere. A tight vertical close-up of a single gang member, the camera placed just off the wearer's left shoulder so we see the head in three-quarter view with the left side of the face nearest the lens; the head is tipped back, chin raised, gazing steeply upward at something enormous above. The balaclava is charcoal grey wool in a chunky rib knit, every stitch and stray fibre crisp, the white ring a raised band of thicker yarn, and the red triangle sharp and off-centre high on the near side of the face, never in the middle. One hand in a dark knitted glove holds the corduroy collar of an olive waxed cotton jacket, today's British high-street clothing. Shot on an 85mm portrait lens wide open at f/1.8: focus lands on the knit around the red triangle and falls away within inches. Low, late-afternoon sun slants in through a sash window off frame to the left, laying a warm honey-gold stripe across the cheek of the mask and picking out the wool texture in raking side light, while the far side of the head drops into soft shadow. Behind and above the figure, filling the top half of the frame, a towering wall of stacked paper reams and loose sheets melts into a soft pale blur; on one sheet near the top, larger than the rest, a bold black printed heading reads THE RULES, slightly soft but readable, the only words in the picture. Colour: warm amber and honey on the mask and jacket against cool, faintly blue paper white behind; natural film-like grain, no glow, no haze, nothing polished.
